name: LM5050MKX-1_NOPB
title: High-side OR-ing FET controller (ideal diode controller for an external N-channel MOSFET)
summary: LM5050-1 and LM5050-1-Q1 drive an external N-channel MOSFET placed in series with a positive supply so that the pair behaves as a diode with a very small forward drop, for OR-ing redundant supplies. An internal charge pump lifts the gate about 12 V above the source, the controller holds the source-to-drain drop near 22 mV at light load, and a comparator pulls the gate down with up to 2 A when current reverses. It works from 5 V to 75 V on IN, OUT and VS (down to 1 V on IN with VS supplied separately), survives 100 V, and comes in a 6-pin thin SOT-23 (DDC).

pins.name: VS
pins.function: Supply for the internal bias circuits and auxiliary supply for the gate charge pump. Usually tied to OUT or IN; a separate 5 V to 75 V supply may feed it instead.

pins.name: OFF
pins.function: Logic input. High pulls GATE low and switches the MOSFET off; current can still flow forward through the MOSFET body diode. Internal 5 µA pulldown; leave open or ground it when not used.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Sense input; connects to the source of the external MOSFET.

pins.name: GATE
pins.function: Gate drive output to the external MOSFET gate, driving it so that the MOSFET acts as a diode with a small forward drop.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Sense input; connects to the drain of the external MOSFET.

circuits.title: Full application
circuits.description: One supply of 5 V to 75 V feeds the load through an N-channel MOSFET whose source is on VIN and drain on VOUT. IN and OUT sense the two ends of the MOSFET and GATE drives its gate. VS takes its supply from VOUT through 100 Ω, filtered by 0.1 µF to ground. The Shutdown input on OFF turns the MOSFET on when low and off when high.

parts.value: Shutdown (low = FET on, high = FET off)

circuits.title: OR-ing with MOSFETs (typical redundant supply configuration)
circuits.description: Two supplies, PS1 and PS2, each reach a shared load bus through their own N-channel MOSFET and LM5050-1. Each controller senses its MOSFET's source on IN and drain on OUT and takes VS from the shared bus. Whichever supply is higher carries the load; the other MOSFET is held off and blocks reverse current. CLOAD and RLOAD stand for the load.

circuits.title: Typical application with input and output transient protection
circuits.description: A 48 V supply feeds the load through Q1, SUM40N10-30, with IN on its source, OUT on its drain and GATE on its gate. CIN (1 µF, 75 V) bypasses the input and D1, an SS16T3 Schottky from ground to VIN, clamps the negative spike at IN when the input is shorted. On the output, COUT (22 µF, 63 V) and D2, an SMBJ60A transient suppressor, absorb the positive spike. VS is fed from VOUT through R1 (100 Ω) with C1 (0.1 µF, 100 V) to ground. OFF/ON drives OFF. Design targets: 6 V to 50 V input, 0 A to 15 A, 0 °C to 50 °C ambient.

circuits.title: Using a separate VS supply for low VIN operation
circuits.description: The rail being OR-ed can be anywhere from 1 V to 75 V because VS is biased from a separate VBIAS supply of 5 V to 75 V through R1 (100), with C3 (0.1 µF, 100 V) to ground. Q1 sits between VIN and VOUT with IN, GATE and OUT on source, gate and drain. C1 (1.0 µF, 100 V) and D1 from ground to VIN protect the input; C2 (22 µF, 100 V) and an 82 V transient suppressor D2 protect the output. Off/On drives OFF.

circuits.title: ORing of two power sources
circuits.description: Two supplies, PS1 and PS2, are OR-ed onto one bus, each through an N-channel MOSFET and an LM5050-1. A transient suppressor from each supply's positive terminal to ground clamps that input. Both VS pins are tied to the common output bus, which carries COUT and the load, CLOAD with RLOAD.

circuits.title: Reverse input voltage protection with IQ reduction
circuits.description: The controller's ground returns through D3 (SS16T3) and a small N-channel MOSFET Q2 (NTR5198NLT3G) whose gate is the ON/OFF control. Turning Q2 off opens the ground path, so the controller draws no current from a battery when it is not needed. D2 (BAS40-7-F) runs from the controller ground node to IN. Q1 (SUM40N10-30) is the pass MOSFET. CIN (1 µF, 75 V) and D1 (SS16T3, ground to VIN) protect the input; Cout (22 µF, 63 V) and D4 (SMBJ60A) protect the output. VS is fed from VOUT through R1 (100 Ω) with C1 (0.1 µF, 100 V) to ground.

circuits.title: Basic application with input transient protection
circuits.description: The simplest protected circuit: Q1 (SUM40N10-30) between VIN (5.0 V to 75 V) and VOUT, IN on its source, OUT on its drain, GATE on its gate, and VS tied straight to VOUT. CIN (1 µF, 100 V) bypasses the input and D1 (B180-13-F Schottky, ground to VIN) clamps negative spikes at IN. OFF/ON drives OFF.

circuits.title: 48-V application with reverse input voltage (VIN = –48 V) protection
circuits.description: A 48 V circuit that survives the input being connected as -48 V. The controller's ground, the anode of D1, the OFF pin and C1 share a local ground that reaches system ground through D3 (SS16T3, anode on the local ground). Q1 (SUM40N10-30) is the pass MOSFET; CIN (1 µF, 75 V) bypasses the input; D1 (SS16T3) clamps IN; COUT (22 µF, 63 V) and D2 (SMBJ60A) protect the output; R1 (100 Ω) and C1 (0.1 µF, 100 V) filter VS from VOUT.

operation.text: A blocking diode in series with a supply, used to OR redundant sources or to guard against reversal, is replaced by an N-channel MOSFET run by the controller, so the forward drop and the power lost in it are much smaller. The source of the MOSFET acts as the anode and the drain as the cathode.

At power-up the load current first flows through the MOSFET body diode. Once the drop across it exceeds VSD(REG), the charge pump starts charging the gate with about 32 µA. The gate rises until an internal 12 V zener from GATE to IN clamps it. At light load the controller lowers the gate so that the source-to-drain drop is held at about 22 mV; at higher load the drop exceeds 22 mV and the gate goes to the 12 V clamp.

When IN falls below OUT by more than VSD(REV) (-28 mV typ), a strong transistor from GATE to IN discharges the gate. The comparator reacts in about 25 ns; the full turn-off time depends on the gate charge, about 180 ns for 47 nF of effective gate capacitance. Until the gate is discharged, the reverse current comes out of the load capacitors and the other supplies in parallel.

VS powers the internal bias and helps supply the charge pump. With inputs above 5 V it can go straight to OUT. When the input sits close to the 5 V minimum, an RC low-pass from OUT to VS (typically 100 Ω, with the smallest capacitor that gives enough filtering, 0.1 µF typical) keeps spikes on IN and OUT from upsetting the part; the resistor is kept small to limit the drop. With VS fed from its own 5 V to 75 V supply, VIN may be as low as 1 V.

operation.topic: Leakage with VS powered and IN floating
operation.text: With VS supplied and IN left open or held at ground, roughly 0.5 mA flows into VS and roughly 3 mA into OUT; about 50 µA of this leaves through IN and the remainder goes to ground. Reliability is not affected. Removing the supply to VS, or opening the controller's ground path with a switch, removes this current.

OFF is a logic input, 5.5 V maximum in operation. High turns the MOSFET off regardless of IN and OUT; load current then flows through the body diode and IN - OUT is about 700 mV. OFF does not disconnect the load because the body diode still conducts. A 5 µA typical pulldown holds it low; if unused it may be left open or grounded.

The figures that matter are continuous drain current ID, body-diode current IS, VDS(MAX), VGS(TH), V(BR)DSS and RDS(ON). ID must exceed the largest continuous load current. VDS(MAX) must withstand the largest differential voltage including faults. In low-voltage designs V(BR)DSS can give OUT some transient protection by conducting back to IN. The recommended choice is a logic-level MOSFET whose RDS(ON) is specified at 5 V gate drive; a sub-logic-level part specified at 2.5 V also works. Lowest RDS(ON) is not always best: a higher RDS(ON) gives the reverse comparator more signal, so turn-off begins at a lower reverse current, and it reduces the small reverse current that can flow without tripping the comparator when supplies are closely matched; low RDS(ON) also costs more. Too high an RDS(ON) wastes power and drives the gate to full voltage, which lengthens turn-off. Aim for 22 mV to 100 mV across the MOSFET at nominal load, and check the MOSFET package thermal resistance since RDS(ON) rises with temperature. The worked example uses SUM40N10-30-E3.

operation.topic: Input short circuit and transient protection
operation.text: A hard short across an input drives the largest reverse current while the gate is being discharged. When the MOSFET turns off, energy in the wiring inductance produces a negative spike at IN and a positive spike at OUT. IN is protected by a diode clamp to ground (a Schottky, for example SS16T3, 1 A 60 V). OUT is protected by a TVS (for example SMBJ60A-13-F), a local bypass capacitor, or both; the output capacitor also absorbs reverse-recovery energy. In low-voltage designs the MOSFET's own breakdown can protect OUT when VIN + V(BR)DSS(MAX) stays below 75 V; few MOSFET makers guarantee a maximum breakdown, though. To keep the part safe under a direct input short, the transients at IN and OUT are clamped with TVS diodes.

Route IN, GATE and OUT close to the MOSFET source, gate and drain. Keep the drain traces wide and short to limit resistive loss. In the example layout with a D2PAK MOSFET, the input suppressor D1 sits beside CIN at the source side and the output suppressor D4 beside COUT at the drain side.
Application note SLVA684 covers stable VGS with LM5050-1 at low current and with a noisy input supply.
